c. 570: Phalaris takes the city. 'Around 570 BC, the city came under the control of Phalaris, a semi-legendary figure'; 'He ruled until around 550 BC'. His territorial campaigns are 'probably anachronistic' on the page.

sources.title: Akragas
sources.note: Founding c. 582-580, Phalaris c. 570-550, expansion between the Platani and the Salso, Heraclea Minoa c. 500, Theron c. 488, Himera 483/480, sack 406, Timoleon, Rome 262/261/210; territory 3,500 km2.

sources.title: Himera
sources.note: Founding 648, Theron's possession and death 472, the Carthaginian destruction of 409.

notes: Classical Akragas only (to the Carthaginian sack of 406, within this group's Archaic and Classical scope). The Hellenistic Akragas (Timoleon's restoration 344-337, Agathokles, the Roman siege 262, capture 261, Carthaginian recapture 255, Treaty of Lutatius, Roman capture 210 and the name Agrigentum) is on the Akragas page and is open for a Sicily gap filler. Population figures on the page range from 16,000-18,000 citizens (de Waele) to 800,000 (Diogenes Laertius, 'far too high'). The page and the Himera page are Wikipedia; the Himera page's founding date 648 is derived from Diodorus's figure. The Himera position is a reading. The early Akragas disc and the Himera disc are coordinate discs (Agrigento at 13.58 E 37.29 N; Himera on the north coast at about 13.83 E 37.97 N) because the gazetteer has no place entries for Agrigento (only the admin-1) or Himera; both names are listed as needed.
